0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="ec46497d6">SOS Foundation is the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) arm of SOS Group of Companies. It was established in 2017 under SOS Pakistan (Pvt.) Ltd. as a not-for-profit organisation. We work to improve the lives of underserved and marginalised communities across Pakistan through sustainable, community-driven development.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="edfc025bd">We are backed by the long-term commitment of SOS Group and our Board of Trustees. This brings corporate discipline, accountability and continuity to our social development work. We work alongside communities, government departments, civil society organisations and international development partners, so that our efforts complement national and provincial priorities.</p></div></div></section><section style="background: #f3ecdc; color: #373b73"><div style="max-width: 1280px; margin: 0 auto; box-sizing: border-box; padding-left: clamp(20px, 4vw, 32px); padding-right: clamp(20px, 4vw, 32px); padding-top: clamp(48px, 8vw, 112px); padding-bottom: clamp(48px, 8vw, 112px)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="display: block; width: 44px; height: 5px; border-radius: 5px; margin-bottom: 20px; background: #59ba53"></span><h2 style="margin: 0; font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: clamp(28.8px, 3.6vw, 46.1px); line-height: 1.14; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #373b73" data-e="e9ece2c60">Our Journey</h2><div style="margin-top: 24px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 20px"><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e16ccb5ec">Education and workforce development have been at the heart of our work since 2017. Through scholarships, teacher training and support for higher education, we have helped young people from low-income households continue their studies and build pathways to dignified employment. flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 20px"><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="ef65985a9">Welcome to SOS Foundation.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e44d3db79">Pakistan's development challenges are well documented, and they demand serious, sustained and collective action. More than 25 million children aged 5 to 16 are out of school, over one-third of that age group¹. Only around 45% of the population uses safely managed drinking water². Female labour force participation stands at just 24.4%³, and the 2022 floods affected 33 million people⁴, a stark reminder of how climate change compounds poverty. Yet with 64% of our population under the age of 30⁵, Pakistan also holds one of the greatest demographic opportunities in the world, if we invest in our people today.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e0a032a15">SOS Foundation exists to help turn that opportunity into reality. Our work is guided by the Constitution of Pakistan, including every child's right to free and compulsory education under Article 25-A, and by the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Every programme we design is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals and with national development priorities, so that our efforts complement those of government and the wider development sector.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="ef6eca23b">We believe development works best when it is led by communities, not delivered to them. We listen first, design solutions together and build local ownership, so that change continues long after our direct involvement ends. Our approach combines grassroots engagement with evidence-based planning, systematic monitoring and transparent reporting, so that every resource entrusted to us delivers verifiable results. Our partnerships with government institutions, universities, civil society, the private sector and development partners allow us to reach further, learn faster and scale what works.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e50d9e607">As Chief Executive Officer, I am committed to leading SOS Foundation with integrity, professionalism and accountability. We will continue to strengthen our programmes, governance and systems in line with recognised standards of good practice in the non-profit sector. We will measure our success not by the activities we carry out but by the lives we help transform, and we will remain open and answerable to the communities, partners and donors who place their trust in us.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e6300e018">I am grateful to our Chairman and Board of Trustees for their vision and guidance, to our dedicated team for their commitment, and to every partner, donor and volunteer who stands with us. I warmly invite you to join us in building a better tomorrow, together.</p></div><div style="margin-top: 32px; padding-top: 20px; border-top: 1px solid #d7d8e3; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px"><p style="margin: 0; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 700" data-e="e0f6c022a">Dr. Abdus Salam</p><p style="margin: 0; font-size: 18px" data-e="ef2961a76">Chief Executive Officer, SOS Foundation</p></div></div></div></div></section></div>

Tariq" style="display: block; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 4 / 5; object-fit: cover; object-position: center top" data-e="ea7197923"></div><div style="flex: 2.4 1 380px; min-width: 0"><span aria-hidden="true" style="display: block; width: 44px; height: 5px; border-radius: 5px; margin-bottom: 20px; background: #59ba53"></span><h2 style="margin: 0; font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: clamp(20.2px, 2.2vw, 27.4px); line-height: 1.29; color: #373b73; letter-spacing: -0.02em" data-e="eff17bef1">Building a better tomorrow, together</h2><div style="margin-top: 24px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 20px"><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e3d500b52">We live in a time of profound global challenges. With 2030 fast approaching, the world remains off track on most of the Sustainable Development Goals. Climate change is intensifying floods, heatwaves and droughts across the globe. Inequality is widening, conflicts and economic shocks are pushing millions back into poverty, and the poorest communities have the fewest means to cope.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e7553ebc1">Pakistan stands at the centre of many of these challenges. We contribute little to global emissions, yet we are among the nations most exposed to climate disasters, as the devastating floods of 2022 made clear. Millions of our children remain out of school, too many families lack safe drinking water and basic healthcare, and many women and young people are still denied the skills and opportunities they need to reach their full potential. At the same time, our young population is our greatest strength. With the right investment, it can become the driving force of a more prosperous and resilient Pakistan.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="ec5713d84">SOS Group of Companies established SOS Foundation in 2017 on a clear conviction: business success carries a responsibility to the society that makes it possible. For us, corporate social responsibility is not charity alone. It is a long-term investment in people, so that they can live with dignity, opportunity and self-reliance. The Foundation brings the discipline, accountability and continuity of the corporate sector to social development, working with government, academia, civil society and the private sector, because no single organisation can meet these challenges alone.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e2c66b1d9">On behalf of the Board of Trustees, I affirm that SOS Foundation will always place the most vulnerable people and communities at the centre of its work. We will uphold the highest standards of integrity, transparency and accountability in the use of every resource entrusted to us, and we will measure our success by the lasting change we help create, not by short-term relief alone. In everything we do, we will contribute to Pakistan's national development priorities and to the global 2030 Agenda, and we will build partnerships that turn shared responsibility into shared progress.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65" data-e="e392fc34a">I thank our partners, donors, volunteers and dedicated team, and above all the communities who place their trust in us. I invite you to join us in building a more equitable, resilient and prosperous future for Pakistan and beyond.</p></div><div style="margin-top: 32px; padding-top: 20px; border-top: 1px solid #d7d8e3; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px"><p style="margin: 0; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 700" data-e="e47bfd3c9">Kanwar M. Women and girls carry much of this burden, often spending long hours fetching water. max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65; font-size: 20px">In Muslim Colony, many women had talent and determination but no training, equipment or way to earn. Some were widows raising children alone, some depended on husbands with irregular daily-wage work, and others had skills they had only ever used at home. SOS Foundation launched stitching and embroidery classes for women and girls, and through a follow-up programme supported by our donors and volunteers, provided sewing machines to women in need.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65; font-size: 20px">What followed was a quiet transformation. Farha, a mother of three who once relied on others for everything, now stitches suits and school uniforms for her neighbours. Her earnings pay for her children's school supplies and help with the rent.</p><blockquote style="margin: 12px 0; padding-left: 28px; border-left: 6px solid #59ba53; max-width: 860px; font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: clamp(20.2px, 2.2vw, 28.8px); line-height: 1.29; letter-spacing: -0.02em">"Earlier, I waited for help with everything. Now I earn for myself." (Farha)</blockquote><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65; font-size: 20px">Nazia, widowed with two young children, now runs a tailoring service from a corner of her home and no longer depends on relatives each month.</p><blockquote style="margin: 12px 0; padding-left: 28px; border-left: 6px solid #59ba53; max-width: 860px; font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: clamp(20.2px, 2.2vw, 28.8px); line-height: 1.29; letter-spacing: -0.02em">"Now my children see that their mother works and earns on her own." (Nazia)</blockquote><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65; font-size: 20px">Sakina turned her gift for embroidery into orders for shawls and bridal suits, and she now teaches the skill to girls on her street. Other women have joined together to take bulk orders from local shops, so a single machine supports several families. One programme has grown into a circle of opportunity that keeps widening.</p><blockquote style="margin: 12px 0; padding-left: 28px; border-left: 6px solid #59ba53; max-width: 860px; font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: clamp(20.2px, 2.2vw, 28.8px); line-height: 1.29; letter-spacing: -0.02em">"What I received, I am now passing on to others." Every visit to the hospital for check-ups and tests meant his son had to hold him up through long corridors, because the hospital’s old wheelchairs were worn out and often already in use. For families already spending on medicines and travel, buying a wheelchair of their own was out of the question.</p><p style="margin: 0; max-width: 820px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.65; font-size: 20px">SOS Foundation, in collaboration with PIMS, donated 30 wheelchairs to the hospital. He reaches his appointments in comfort, and his family no longer has to struggle to carry him.
